newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds higher on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bond prices closed higher across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest following a drop in the interbank rate, dealers said on Friday.

"Bond prices were marked up slightly today as the interbank rate fell sharply on some speculative activity ahead of the weekend. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.80/98.85 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.36/98.41 and September 2001 at S$97.75/97.80 against S$97.54/97.59.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 1 0-7/8 percent versus Thursday's 2-5/8 2-1/4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.13/1.08 percent against Thursday's yield of 1.70/1.65 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.70/1.65 percent from 2.00/1.95 percent.
